# Redis Fleet Tracker Extension

Reports a collector fleet's live member count, backed by Redis, so components can scale a per-instance budget by fleet size.

Counts the collector instances currently alive in a "fleet" using a Redis
sorted set, and lets other components subscribe to that count. Built for
consumers that scale a per-instance budget by fleet size, most directly the
`adaptive_tail_sampling` processor, which divides each `adaptive_throughput`
rule's `goal_throughput` by the live count
([contrib#51544](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/pull/51544)).

Only sorted-set and expiry commands are used, so API-compatible servers work.
Verified against Redis 7 and Valkey 8.

> [!WARNING]
> Development stability. The configuration may still change.

## Configuration

```yaml
extensions:
  redis_fleet_tracker:
    endpoint: redis:6379         # required, host:port
    username: ${env:REDIS_USER}  # optional, for ACL auth
    password: ${env:REDIS_PW}    # optional
    db: 0                        # optional, Redis logical database
    tls:
      insecure: true             # optional, default true (plain TCP)
    fleet: ${env:DEPLOY_ENV}  # optional, see "Fleet scoping" below
    key_prefix: fleet_tracker # optional, default fleet_tracker
    heartbeat_interval: 3s    # optional, default 3s
    ttl: 10s                  # optional, default 10s, must exceed heartbeat_interval

service:
  extensions: [redis_fleet_tracker]
```

| Field | Default | Required | Description |
|-------|---------|----------|--------------|
| `endpoint` | - | yes | Redis server address, `host:port`. |
| `username` | `""` | no | Redis ACL username (Redis 6 and later). Leave unset for password-only auth. |
| `password` | `""` | no | Redis auth password. |
| `db` | `0` | no | Redis logical database number. |
| `tls` | `insecure: true` | no | TLS settings for the Redis connection. Disabled (plain TCP) by default; set `tls::insecure: false` to opt in. |
| `fleet` | the extension's own component ID | no | The group of instances counted together. See "Fleet scoping" below. |
| `key_prefix` | `fleet_tracker` | no | Namespaces every key this extension writes. |
| `heartbeat_interval` | `3s` | no | How often this instance refreshes its membership. |
| `ttl` | `10s` | no | How long a member is considered live after its last heartbeat. Must be greater than `heartbeat_interval`. |

## Using it with `adaptive_tail_sampling`

Name this extension in the processor's `fleet_tracker` setting. The processor
resolves it by method shape, so neither side imports the other.

```yaml
extensions:
  redis_fleet_tracker:
    endpoint: redis:6379

processors:
  adaptive_tail_sampling:
    fleet_tracker: redis_fleet_tracker
    rules:
      - name: throughput-cap
        sampler:
          type: adaptive_throughput
          goal_throughput: 1000   # fleet-wide budget; divided by the live member count

service:
  extensions: [redis_fleet_tracker]
  pipelines:
    traces:
      processors: [adaptive_tail_sampling]
```

Only `adaptive_throughput` rules are affected, since percentage-based samplers
already compose across instances without division.

The processor's
[Fleet-wide throughput budget](../../../processor/adaptivetailsamplingprocessor/README.md#fleet-wide-throughput-budget-fleet_tracker)
section covers the division and its caveats, including integer division and
the per-instance floor of 1 span/s. One worth repeating here. A collector
counts as one fleet member however many pipelines it runs, but each
pipeline's samplers target the divided goal independently, so run the fleet
budget in one pipeline only.

## Fleet scoping

`fleet` names the group counted together and defaults to the extension's own
component ID, so instances with identical config count together.

To share one Redis across environments, give each a distinct `fleet`, e.g.
`fleet: ${env:DEPLOY_ENV}`. Named instances such as
`redis_fleet_tracker/prod` already scope themselves through the component ID
and need no `fleet` setting. `key_prefix` and `db` separate the keyspace
further when you want test keys kept clear of production ones.

Fleet collisions fail in one direction. Two fleets that should be separate
inflate the observed count, which under-samples wherever that count feeds a
per-instance budget.

## Data model

One Redis sorted set per fleet, key `<key_prefix>:<fleet>`. Each heartbeat
tick pipelines:

```
ZADD    <key>  <now_ms + ttl_ms>  <member_id>   # register/refresh self
ZREMRANGEBYSCORE <key>  -inf  <now_ms>          # prune expired members
ZCARD   <key>                                    # live member count
PEXPIRE <key>  <2 * ttl_ms>                      # dead-fleet key self-cleans
```

Registering self happens before pruning, so self is always counted even if
its own previous heartbeat expired. `member_id` is the first 16 hex
characters of `sha256(service.instance.id)`, or a random UUID generated at
startup when that attribute is unset. Hostnames and pod names are
deliberately not used, since they get reused across restarts and the new
instance would be indistinguishable from the old one.

The collector generates a unique `service.instance.id` per process, so the
default needs no attention. If you pin it under `service.telemetry.resource`,
keep it unique per instance. Instances sharing one share a `member_id` and
count as a single member, so the fleet undercounts and over-delivers against
any budget derived from the count. A pod name or hostname is fine, a constant
or a deployment-wide value is not.

On shutdown, the extension makes a best-effort `ZREM <key> <member_id>` with
a short timeout before closing the Redis client.

## Failure semantics

- **Start-anyway**: `Start` attempts one synchronous heartbeat (~3s
  timeout) to prime the count, but returns `nil` regardless of whether it
  succeeds. A Redis outage at startup does not block collector startup;
  background heartbeats keep retrying.
- Consumers hold the last-good count until the next successful heartbeat;
  nothing is delivered to `SubscribeMemberCount` until a count is known.
- **Clock skew**: member expiry is computed from each instance's own clock.
  Skew beyond `ttl` can transiently prune a still-live member; it
  re-registers on its next heartbeat, so the effect is a brief undercount,
  not a stuck one.

## The SubscribeMemberCount contract

```go
type fleetTracker interface {
	SubscribeMemberCount(callback func(count int)) (cancel func(), err error)
}
```

Consumers assert this interface structurally against the extension retrieved
via `host.GetExtensions`, so no shared package is required. The callback
fires once a count is known and again whenever it changes, and must not
block. Deliveries are serialised against each other, all made from one
goroutine. `cancel` unsubscribes and is idempotent, though one in-flight
delivery may still complete after it returns.
